title: Measles Outbreak Kills 83 Samoans, Mostly Children
reason: The 2019 Samoa measles outbreak (September/October-December 2019, epidemic emergency running into January 2020) is confirmed by multiple independent sources. By 6 January 2020, over 5,700 cases and 83 deaths were reported in a population of ~200,874 (under 200,000 threshold roughly matches). The great majority of deaths were children under five (61 of first 70 deaths were age 4 and under; all but seven of all deaths were under 15). Low MMR coverage (dropped from ~74-75% in 2017 to ~31-40% in 2018) driven by a 2013 vaccination scandal (two infant deaths from improperly mixed MMR vaccine, causing a 10-month program suspension) and subsequent misinformation/mistrust is confirmed as the core cause. Samoa declared a state of emergency on 15 November 2019 and ran a mass vaccination campaign with international EMT support, which brought the outbreak under control. All material details (country, year, case/death counts, cause, response) match.

title: Tuilaepa Pushes Three Controversial Constitutional Bills
reason: Independent sources confirm all material details. Samoa's Parliament passed three bills — the Constitution Amendment Bill 2020, Land and Titles Bill 2020, and Judicature Bill 2020 — on 15 December 2020 (vote 41-4), under PM Tuilaepa Sailele Malielegaoi's HRPP government. The bills restructured the judiciary, creating a parallel Land and Titles High Court/Court of Appeal for customary land and titles (matai) matters and removing appeals to the ordinary Supreme Court/Court of Appeal. Critics — Samoa's judiciary, the Samoa Law Society, the government's own Ombudsman, the UN Special Rapporteur on judicial independence, and Amnesty International — warned the reforms eroded judicial independence and violated ICCPR Article 14. The controversy caused several ruling-party MPs (including Deputy PM Fiame Naomi Mata'afa) to resign, directly feeding the backlash that shaped the 2021 election, which HRPP historically lost. Country, year, and substance all confirmed.

title: Cyclone Ofa Devastates Samoa
reason: Cyclone Ofa did hit Samoa (Western Samoa) on Feb 1-4, 1990, killing 7 people there (8 total across the region), leaving ~25,000 homeless and damaging/destroying over 10,000 homes out of a population of 170,000 — confirming country, year, and the death/housing-damage narrative. However, the damage figure is overstated: every independent source found (Wikipedia citing the Fiji Met Service report, UPI's 1990 wire report, Samoa Global News) consistently puts total damage at roughly US$180-187 million region-wide (Samoa + American Samoa combined), with Samoa's own share at ~US$130-150 million — not 'over USD 200 million' as described. No source supports a >$200M figure for Ofa alone; the only $200M figure found in searches belongs to the unrelated 2018 Cyclone Gita. GDP impact is corroborated in spirit (Ofa+Val combined caused Samoa's GDP to fall ~50% 1989-1991), so 'huge share of GDP' holds, but the specific dollar magnitude claimed is materially inflated by roughly 35-50% versus the best-documented figures.
